notes:
**Document and content (134-1.004.note.document).** A letter headed “Lodève le 27.”, followed by an obscured date group retained as `\unsure{8.74|8/74|8/4}`, addresses Deligne. The opening considers a first-cycle course in the first trimester and a small algebra seminar on Mme Sinh’s “fourbis”, transposed to “champs”. The cause phrase remains damaged; the following noun is best read as `\unsure{faute}`. The separate sideways hand addresses Breen, asks “Qu’en pens-tu.”, closes “Bien à toi”, and signs P. with a surname retained as uncertain Deligne. Archive foliation is 61; there is no author page number.

**Mathematics and author qualifications (134-1.004.text.triangle).** For abelian sheaves M,N on a topos X, the page names a truncated derived underlined Hom expression E(M,N), gives two cohomology rows, and proposes a three-object triangle with underlined Hom(M,{}_2N)[-2] at its apex. The author explicitly says “qui pour l’instant reste heuristique” and “il doit y avoir un triangle distingué canonique”. No proof of this triangle is supplied or certified here.

**Reading prompted by mathematics (134-1.004.check.truncation; 134-1.004.text.exponents).** The degree bound 0≤i≤2 made the ≤/< subscript worth inspecting. By the meaning of truncation, ≤2 retains degree 2 whereas <2 cuts it off; this is a consistency check only. The crop independently shows the short lower comparison stroke and supports ≤2. The first H exponent has a detached dot and resolves to i. The second has a left hook without a distinct dot, so `\unsure{j|i}` remains even though the same row’s condition uses i. The live Ext has an overwritten underlying term, tentatively Hom, which H omits. The double-stem R and underlines are retained. These are visual reading decisions, not a proof of the proposed construction.

**Preserved spelling and marks.** The margin’s unaccented “repondre” and shortened “pens-tu.” are retained; “neamoins/neanmoins” and the accent in “maître/maitre” remain uncertain. A small isolated point after “pour”, missed by both witnesses and two readers, is included with doubt because it may be a reproduction speck.
